Cucuto runs a small module inside system_server, the core of Android. That is what makes it reliable, and also what makes it risky.
A bug in a system module can crash Android or stop the phone from booting. Cucuto catches every error and falls back to WhatsApp\'s tone, but no code is perfect.
Root and LSPosed weaken Android\'s security and can break banking apps, Google Play Integrity and your warranty. That is true of every LSPosed module.
An Android update can move the code Cucuto hooks. The module then stops swapping sounds and WhatsApp\'s tone plays until Cucuto is updated.
To pick a voice, the module reads who sent each WhatsApp notification (name and chat ID). That stays in Cucuto\'s private storage on this phone.
Know how to recover before you enable it: the install guide explains how to turn the module or LSPosed off if the phone does not boot.
Open the LSPosed manager, go to Modules and turn on Cucuto. Its scope is System Framework, already selected. Do not add WhatsApp or any other app: Cucuto never hooks them.
